newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cash JGBs sold after release of output data.
newsitem.headline: Cash JGBs sold after release of output data.

text.p: The yield of the benchmark 182nd cash Japanese government bond rose slightly on Thursday after the release of industrial output data at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT).
Forecasts for Japan manufacturers' output in December and January were stronger than expected, and invited slight selling of cash JGBs, a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB yield stood at 2.510 percent as of 0650 GMT, up from previous day's 2.460 percent.
The yield of the benchmark JGB stood at 2.495 percent at 0623 GMT, minutes before the output data was released.

The Ministry of International Trade and Ministry on Thursday forecast Japan manufacturers' output in December to rise by 0.8 percent month-on-month, and output in January to increase by 5.1 percent month-on-month.
MITI also said Japan's industrial production fell a preliminary 1.9 percent in November from the previous month.
The figure, however, was within market's expectations and had little effect on JGBs, the trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
Earlier, the key March JGB futures ended sharply down due to a plunge in Tokyo share prices, traders said.

This is because few players are eager to be on the receiving side of trades in the IRS market, while JGBs are supported on the downside as some investors remain eager to buy cash bonds on dips, the trader said.
However, some investors have been detected buying put options, and this may cause JGBs to have a downward bias toward the start of the New Year, the trader added.
